name: Benjamin Mackovak
current_role: Co-Founder & Managing Member, Strategic Value Bank Partners (Cleveland); director on several community-bank boards (First Foundation director since 2024)
profile: Ohio-based bank investor who co-founded Strategic Value Bank Partners in 2015, an investment partnership specialising in community banks. Through activist/strategic stakes he sits on bank boards including First Foundation (joined 2024 via SVBP investment agreement), BankFinancial and Idaho First Bank. Earlier founded Cavalier Capital.
interesting_fact: Discussed the 'secret sauce' of investing in small community banks, bank failures and fintech on The Meb Faber Show (episode #519).
deep_cut_fact: Began his career at Merrill Lynch, then worked at Newport Beach large-cap manager First American Trust and as senior analyst at Charlottesville hedge fund Rivanna Capital; Kent State BA magna cum laude, UVA Darden MBA.
notes: Low public profile; no published firm website/email found (svbpartners.com shows 'Coming Soon'). SEC data suggests First Foundation position disposed/delisted around April 2026 (possibly via merger) - verify. Best route is likely via bank boards or podcast appearances.

name: Jonathan J Doyle
current_role: Vice Chairman, Senior Managing Principal & Head of Financial Services Group, Piper Sandler; director, nCino
profile: Veteran bank M&A and capital-raising banker. Was senior managing principal at Sandler O'Neill + Partners, which Piper Jaffray acquired in January 2020 to form Piper Sandler; now runs its financial services group and sits on its leadership team and board. Also a director of bank-software company nCino since around 2019-2020.
interesting_fact: Sits on the board of nCino, the cloud banking software company, while leading one of the largest bank M&A advisory franchises in the US.
deep_cut_fact: A William & Mary finance graduate, he is a trustee emeritus of the College of William & Mary Foundation and serves on the board of The Governor's Academy in Byfield, Massachusetts.
notes: Private-leaning banker; route via Piper Sandler media relations (Nick Lawler).

name: Cosmo Feilding-Mellen
current_role: Co-Founder and Director, AtaiBeckley Inc. (formerly Co-Founder & CEO, Beckley Psytech)
profile: British biotech entrepreneur, son of psychedelic-research pioneer Amanda Feilding. Co-founded Beckley Research & Innovations (2016), Beckley Canopy Therapeutics and, in 2019, Beckley Psytech to develop psychedelic medicines (e.g. BPL-003 5-MeO-DMT nasal spray). atai took a stake and later merged with Beckley Psytech to form AtaiBeckley, where he is a director.
interesting_fact: Beckley Psytech's 5-MeO-DMT nasal spray (BPL-003) for depression reached a successful FDA end-of-Phase 2 meeting, with Phase 3 planned for 2026 at AtaiBeckley.
deep_cut_fact: Says that at a school drug-education workshop aged about 13-14, his classmates' answers to a question about drugs all named his mother - an upbringing he says took the 'exciting act of rebellion' out of drugs and made him more sensible about them.
notes: A July 2026 SEC filing mentions a pending transaction involving Lilly and Nualtis, so company contacts may change. Has done podcasts (e.g. Power to the Patients).

name: Cameron M Bready
current_role: President & CEO, Global Payments Inc.; director, Crawford & Company
profile: Atlanta-based payments executive. Joined Global Payments in 2014 as CFO, became President & COO in 2019 and CEO in June 2023. Before payments he spent years in energy: Northeast Utilities, Mirant, then CFO of electric transmission utility ITC Holdings (2009-2014).
interesting_fact: Came to fintech from the power sector - he was CFO of ITC Holdings, the largest independent US electric transmission company, before joining Global Payments; a natural energy/payments crossover guest.
deep_cut_fact: An Oglethorpe University business graduate, he now chairs Oglethorpe's board of trustees and is also a trustee of Pace Academy in Atlanta.
notes: Busy large-cap CEO; route via Global Payments corporate communications / IR. Business Roundtable member.

name: Michael J Kasbar
current_role: Executive Chairman, World Kinect Corporation (operating as World Fuel)
profile: Co-founder of marine-fuel broker Trans-Tec Services (c.1985) with Paul Stebbins, sold to the predecessor of World Fuel Services in 1995. Rose to CEO (2012-Dec 2025) and Chairman (2014), building the company into a global energy/fuel logistics and sustainability services group (renamed World Kinect). Became Executive Chairman when Ira Birns took over as CEO in January 2026.
interesting_fact: Turned a small New York bunker-brokerage startup into a Fortune 500 global fuel and energy services company, taking most of the 1995 sale consideration in stock.
deep_cut_fact: Graduated early from SUNY Plattsburgh with an environmental science degree, 'having no idea of what he really wanted to do,' and fell into the marine fuel broking business in New York soon after.
notes: Strong fit for energy podcast (fuel logistics, energy transition services). Some 2026 releases use investor@worldfuel.com instead. Founding year given as 1984 in some sources.

name: W Kirk Wycoff
current_role: Managing Partner, Patriot Financial Partners (Radnor, PA); Lead Independent Director, USCB Financial Holdings
profile: Pennsylvania bank investor and former bank CEO. Led Crusader Savings Bank and then Progress Financial Corp. as chairman/CEO (1991-2004), later Continental Bank, and co-founded private-equity firm Patriot Financial Partners (c.2006-07), which invests in community banks and fintechs. Its stake makes him a 10% owner of Miami's USCB Financial, where he is lead independent director.
interesting_fact: Patriot Financial Partners took the lead investor role in launching Ampersand, a Midwest fintech platform for deposit-management strategies.
deep_cut_fact: A Franklin & Marshall College business/finance graduate who has served as an F&M trustee, and a presenter to the TIGER 21 investor peer network.
notes: Legal first name Walter. Has appeared as a contributor on the 'Plugged In' podcast (buzzsprout).

name: Scott R. Lovett
current_role: President, Go To Market, Fastly (announced Nov 2026 he plans to retire in 2027, then Senior Advisor)
profile: Enterprise security/CDN sales leader. SVP Global Web & Security Sales at Akamai (2018-21), CRO at Imperva (2021-24), then joined edge-cloud company Fastly as CRO in Aug 2024 and was promoted to President, Go To Market in Aug 2025, uniting sales and marketing. Fastly announced on Nov 4, 2026 that he plans to retire in 2027.
interesting_fact: Has spent much of his career selling the internet's plumbing - CDN and web security - at three of its main players: Akamai, Imperva and Fastly.
deep_cut_fact: Holds a BA in Communications from Eastern Illinois University rather than a technical or business degree.
notes: Transitioning to retirement in 2027 - may have more time for interviews; edge/data-infrastructure angle fits data-center podcast.

name: Raul E Cesan
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Commercial Worldwide LLC; independent director, Gartner Inc. (since 2012)
profile: Former pharmaceutical executive who spent ~25 years at Schering-Plough, rising to President & COO (1998-2001). Founded investment firm Commercial Worldwide LLC in 2001 and has served on boards including The New York Times Company (until 2018), Chiasma (chairman) and Gartner, where he sits on the compensation committee.
interesting_fact: Served nearly two decades on the board of The New York Times Company (1999-2018) while also being a long-time Gartner director.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Schering-Plough's US pharma business, he headed Schering-Plough International (1988-1992), spending 25 years at the company in total.
notes: Very private, now in his late 70s; no published personal or firm contact found. Route via Gartner corporate secretary/IR if needed. Gartner bio page blocks scripted access.
